title: Redwood POC weekly sync - benchmark review vs baseline provider
summary: Weekly POC sync to review latency and throughput benchmarks vs their current baseline provider. Redwood showed updated runs with batching and KV-cache enabled; overall p50 improved, p95 on some tails still higher than baseline in the largest sequence length tests. Discussed tuning (batch sizes, quantization), infra differences, and next steps to provision extra dedicated capacity and share raw logs/benchmark spreadsheet.
topics: Dedicated vs hosted routing for peak traffic
Action items and next steps: logs, extra infra, security docs

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-02 10:00 PDT / 17:00Z
Duration: 45 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Maya Lin (Redwood CSM); Jon Bates (AstraHealth CTO), Priya Nair (AstraHealth ML), Liam O'Connor (AstraHealth SRE), Renee Park (AstraHealth Product)

Summary (auto): quick recap of last week, ran extended benchmark with batching + KV cache. overall wins on median latency, some tail regressions on big sequences.

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, um we have about 45 minutes. quick agenda, we'll run through the updated benchmark csv that i sent this morning, go over raw logs, then propose the infra steps for the stress tests.
[00:22] Jon Bates: yep thanks alex, we really wanna see where you landed vs VendorX, last week the baseline p95 was lower for us so curious.
[00:35] Samira Khan: hi all, i pushed the runs into the shared sheet - link in the chat - and annotated the runs where we changed batch windows and enabled prefix kv cache. quick note, transcription in the sheet says "KV cache" but some rows show K V cache in the raw tool's name because of the exporter naming.
[00:50] Priya Nair: ok cool, we'll pull it up. question, how comparable is your infra to our baseline? is VendorX using the same GPU family?
[01:05] Diego Morales: good q. short answer: not identical. VendorX runs on A100S with a different kernel stack; our dedicated pods for you are running H100V2 variant this week. that said the model variants are aligned - same quantization profile we used as agreed.
[01:28] Liam O'Connor: H100V2, ok, did you change the kernel selection? last run i recall you used default kernels which slightly differ in mem layout.
[01:40] Samira Khan: yeah we updated the compile flags and selected the low-latency kernel set for the long-seq tests. also turned on continuous batching with 100ms window for a subset of runs.
[01:55] Renee Park: can you remind us of the key metrics in the sheet?
[02:05] Alex Chen: sure - p50, p95, p99 latencies and tokens/s throughput. the baseline vendor is marked in column B as VendorX-20260830. our runs are labeled Redwood-20260901-.. . we did three primary sweeps: small seq (<=128), med (129-512), large (512+).
[02:28] Priya Nair: pulling it up now... oh i see, for small seq p50 you are about 20-25% faster, p95 about even. med seq you're slightly better on throughput. for large seq p95 looks worse than VendorX on two of the runs. that matches what jon saw.
[02:52] Samira Khan: correct, the large seq tail is what we flagged - it's likely due to memory copy patterns in the long-kv chain and how our batcher interacts under high concurrency. we think 2 fixes: bump batch window to 120ms or enable local prefix-only cache on those pods to reduce KV lookups.
[03:15] Jon Bates: any tradeoffs? if we bump to 120ms our 95% latency SLO might break for real-time features.
[03:25] Alex Chen: yes exactly tradeoff between tail latency and throughput/cost. with 120ms you'll get higher tokens/s and lower avg cost, but p95 may increase. alternatively we can provision dedicated nodes for high concurrency paths so you get both low p95 and good throughput at higher cost.
[03:45] Priya Nair: what's the delta in cost if we provision two extra dedicated pods?
[03:50] Diego Morales: approximate math in the sheet - about 18-22% uplift in monthly committed cost for the POC test window, but for production we can optimize by compressing KV entries and using 4-bit quantization which lowers GPU footprint.
[04:12] Liam O'Connor: did you try the quantized runs? i thought we asked for 4-bit profile.
[04:18] Samira Khan: yes we did Q4 runs in column F - note the Q4 p50 is slightly higher than fp16 for some med seqs, but cost is lower. for long sequences the quantization sometimes increases tail due to dequantization overheads, we need to tune kernels.
[04:40] Renee Park: can you show a specific example?
[04:44] Samira Khan: sure, look at Redwood-20260901-Large-Q4-run3: p50 310ms, p95 1.8s vs VendorX-Large-run2 p50 330ms, p95 1.4s. so median is good but tail worse.
[05:05] Jon Bates: those p95 numbers are important because our compliance team flags anything over 1.5s for interactive flows.
[05:15] Alex Chen: noted. question for priya: is the 1.5s p95 hard requirement across all flows or only for interactive product?
[05:24] Priya Nair: interactive yes, async batch flows are okay with higher tails. most of our user-facing features are interactive.
[05:32] Alex Chen: ok so we should focus tests on the interactive distribution.
[05:38] Diego Morales: on logs, we noticed a couple of spikes correlated with garbage-collection cycles in one of the infra nodes; i have the raw server logs in the folder - there is some noise that may have worsened p95 on 9/01 run.
[05:53] Liam O'Connor: can you share that exact log slice? we'll compare with our monitoring.
[05:58] Diego Morales: yes sending.
[06:05] Samira Khan: also wanted to caveat the exporter - the transcription in the csv sometimes shows slightly different metric windows; i normalized but raw traces are attached in a tar.gz.
[06:18] Renee Park: great. next question: network egress/cold-starts - any obvious differences?
[06:25] Diego Morales: for cold-starts we saw 100-150ms extra in our hosted cold path, but your dedicated nodes are warm for the POC runs. egress peering could add 30-80ms depending on region; that's in the note at the top of the sheet.
[06:40] Jon Bates: VendorX is peered in our region so their network is slightly faster, that could explain tails.
[06:46] Samira Khan: agreed. we can run a peered test in your VPC to match baseline networking and re-run the large-seq stress test.
[06:56] Priya Nair: that would be helpful. can you also capture the p99? we need to see worst-case tail.
[07:03] Alex Chen: yep we'll include p99 and raw latencies for the next run.
[07:10] Renee Park: about the security docs - your security team asked for SOC2 / iso attestation and KMS integration notes. have those been shared?
[07:20] Maya Lin: we shared a redwood-security-pack link last week, but i'll resend the full pack and a short summary addressing KMS, VPC peering, audit logs retention.
[07:30] Jon Bates: make sure to include the HSM options and audit log TTL.
[07:35] Maya Lin: will do.
[07:40] Priya Nair: any thoughts on routing policy? we saw some requests forwarded to the hosted fallback; is that expected?
[07:48] Samira Khan: yes by default our smart routing will fallback to hosted variants when dedicated capacity saturates; for the POC we left it enabled to avoid errors. we can disable fallback and fail fast if you want to measure dedicated-only behavior.
[08:05] Liam O'Connor: disable fallback for the next dedicated stress test, please. we want an apples-to-apples run.
[08:10] Alex Chen: noted, we'll run a dedicated-only sweep.
[08:16] Diego Morales: timeline: we can provision two extra dedicated pods by 2026-09-07. after that we propose a 4-hour stress window to reproduce the tail under traffic. we'll collect p50/p95/p99 and token/s.
[08:33] Jon Bates: sounds good. for the stress window please include our SREs so we can correlate our metrics.
[08:39] Alex Chen: absolutely.
[08:44] Priya Nair: one more thing - can you send the raw prompt templates? they might be causing longer decode graphs for some sequences.
[08:52] Samira Khan: already on the sheet under artifacts, but i'll export them separately as text files.
[08:58] Renee Park: ok wrap up?
[09:01] Alex Chen: quick recap: 1) Alex will send updated benchmark CSV + raw logs and include p99 by 2026-09-04; 2) Samira will request 2 extra dedicated GPU pods and disable hosted fallback for the stress window, target provisioning 2026-09-07; 3) Priya will share production request distribution and prompt templates by 2026-09-06; 4) Maya will resend security pack and KMS/HSM notes by 2026-09-04; 5) schedule deep dive on 2026-09-09 with SREs.
[09:22] Jon Bates: thanks folks, appreciate the quick turn.
[09:26] Alex Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up in the shared thread. bye.
